subject: Joint run specification and reproducibility checklist
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Joint run specification and reproducibility checklist

Alex — thanks for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can scope the joint benchmark run. TL;DR: we need the canonical prompt set, a runnable harness link (or a reproducible mapping), concrete streaming semantics, and target SLOs (p95/p99 token and end-to-end).

Key facts from call (please correct if I missed anything):
- Workload: chat-style streaming assistant for checkout flows; expected steady-state 300 qps, occasional spikes to 1k qps; 200 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions.
- Prompt profile: 60% short requests (~20 tokens), 40% medium (~180 tokens) with an average generated response length ~250 tokens.
- Target SLOs: customer stated desire for token-latency p95 <= 200ms and end-to-end turnaround p95 <= 350ms for typical sessions; they also asked about graceful degradation when bursts hit 1k qps.

Deliverables Redwood will produce for the joint run:
1) Benchmark matrix (attached) that enumerates run types, measurement windows, and expected metrics.
2) A reproducibility checklist that documents warm/cold definitions, tokenization, model seed/quant flags, and kernel configs used.
3) Mapping guide to translate Redwood harness metrics to your internal harness counters (we'll do a dry-run mapping pass before the joint test).

Asks for FastCommerce before we run:
- Canonical prompt set for the qualification (the small sample prompts you mentioned; attach as a JSON or share a Drive link).
- Link to your test harness or a reproducible interface (if you can't share the harness, provide a recording of request/response pairs + arrival patterns).
- Confirmation of which latency metric matters most: first-byte token latency vs last-byte / end-of-response. We'll measure both, but we need to prioritize.
- Any additional constraints: KV cache warm-up expectations, per-customer isolation needs, and acceptable quantization knobs (if you have preferences).

Proposed test plan (high-level):
- Run A: Cold start profile (3x restarts, quick 5-minute ramp)
- Run B: Warm steady-state (30 minutes sustained at target qps)
- Run C: Burst stress (spike to 1k qps for 10 minutes, observe fallbacks/failover behavior)

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_prompts_fastcommerce.json (prompt sampler).

Next steps: if you can share the prompt JSON and a harness link by EOD Tue (PST), we can schedule a joint execution window Wed-Fri next week. Otherwise suggest two windows and we'll pick one.

Thanks — looking forward to validating the SLOs with you.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@fastcommerce.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Joint run specification and reproducibility checklist

Vivek — thanks for the write-up and the clear asks. Confirming items from our side and adding clarifications:

Workload details (from infra):
- Sustained target: 300 qps (as you wrote).
- Spike profile: short bursts to 1k qps lasting up to 10 minutes based on marketing campaigns.
- Streaming sessions: ~200 concurrent connections; each session issues a 2–6 message exchange where the server streams tokens back.
- Token characteristics: average model response ~250 tokens; roughly 60% of requests have small context (<= 40 tokens).

SLO clarification:
- Primary SLO for the feature team is perceived latency: they care most about first-token latency for streaming (so user sees a response start quickly). The numbers we want to validate: p95 first-token latency <= 220ms, p99 first-token <= 450ms. End-to-end p95 <= 400ms is a softer goal.

Repro data we can share:
- Prompt pack (attached): sample_prompts_fastcommerce.json — small representative set.
- Internal harness: we can't share the raw harness binary, but here's a reproducible trace and a small harness shim on Drive that replays arrival patterns: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-harness-link
- We also have an internal SLO doc (DocSend): https://docsend.com/f/fastcommerce-slo

Question: how does Redwood measure "first-token latency" for streaming? Do you count time from request arrival to the first byte emitted on the stream? Also curious whether your harness supports deterministic tokenization (we need repeatable runs across different hardware).

We can make the prompt pack available right now. For scheduling a joint run, Wed 11am–2pm PST or Thu 3pm–6pm PST both work for the infra lead. Let us know which you prefer.

Regards,
Alex
Alex Torres
Sr. Product Manager — Checkout
FastCommerce Inc.

Attachments: sample_prompts_fastcommerce.json (prompt sampler)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 20:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Joint run specification and reproducibility checklist

Alex — perfect, thanks for the prompt pack and the harness replay link. Answers inline and a few small tweaks to the test plan so we measure exactly what you care about.

How we measure first-token latency (Redwood harness):
- First-token latency: measured from request enqueue (timestamp when request hits the front of the serving queue) to the timestamp when the first token bytes are emitted on the response stream. We capture both router-side enqueue and node-side receive timestamps so we can separate network vs runtime.
- End-to-end: measured from client request timestamp (we'll use the replay arrival times you provided) to last-token emitted.

Reproducibility and determinism:
- Tokenization: we will use the same tokenizer binary as your harness; if you can confirm tokenizer version/hash we will lock that.
- Model determinism: we'll set sampling deterministic (no temperature/random sampling) for qualification runs and record the model seed/weight shims in the reproducibility checklist.
- Quantization/kernels: we'll include the exact compilation flags, quant format (e.g., 4-bit q8_0 or q4_K_M), and kernel build IDs in the artifact we share.

Updated test plan (deltas in bold):
- Run A (Cold): 3x restarts. For each restart we do a 10-minute ramp to target qps and measure the first 5 minutes for cold effects.
- Run B (Warm-steady): 30-minute sustained at 300 qps; measure moving p50/p95/p99 of first-token and end-to-end latency in 1-minute windows.
- Run C (Burst): spike to 1k qps for 10 minutes; observe fallback behavior, queuing, and any model fallbacks to cheaper variants.

Additional items we will produce and share pre-run:
- A reproducibility manifest (text file) capturing binary hashes, kernel IDs, model artifact id, quant flags.
- A mapping doc that maps our metric names to the ones in your replay shim (so you can correlate traces).

Scheduling: Wed 11:00–13:00 PST works for our infra team. Let's lock Wed — please confirm and we'll generate the shared run calendar invite (we'll include run owners: Vivek (owner), Rishi (run engineer), Monica (customer success)).

One small ask for legal/compliance: we will keep request/response logs for 14 days for debugging and then auto-delete; does that match your data retention policy for this exercise? If you need an NDA/scoped data agreement, please loop in your legal.

—
Vivek
